evidence.quote: Swinerton Builders (“Contractor”)
evidence.rationale: The contractor is named in the agreement preamble.

evidence.quote: This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of California
evidence.rationale: The governing law clause names California.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor understands that all payments to Subcontractor will be made only from a special fund and a specific source, namely, from payments made by Owner from time to time to Contractor in respect of work performed by Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Payments come only from the owner's payments, so the subcontractor bears the risk of owner non-payment. However, 6(b) frames its conditions precedent as relating to 'the time for payment', and 6(b)(i) requires payment with interest if the non-payment is due to Contractor's breach. The provisions are mixed, so the classification is uncertain.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall make payments to Subcontractor within seven (7) days after receipt by Contractor of payment from Owner for the work of Subcontractor for which payment has been made
evidence.rationale: The clause states seven days after Contractor receives the owner's payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall make payments to Subcontractor within seven (7) days after receipt by Contractor of payment from Owner for the work of Subcontractor for which payment has been made
evidence.rationale: A specific payment period is written into the contract.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall retain from progress or other payments hereunder ten percent (10%) of the amount due
evidence.rationale: Retention of 10% equals 1000 bps.

release_condition.value: after final acceptance of the work by the Architect and Owner and until ten (10) days after Contractor’s receipt of final retention payment from Owner

evidence.quote: until after final acceptance of the work by the Architect and Owner and until ten (10) days after Contractor’s receipt of final retention payment from Owner
evidence.rationale: The release condition is stated plainly in 6(c).

evidence.quote: until ten (10) days after Contractor’s receipt of final retention payment from Owner
evidence.rationale: Ten days after Contractor receives the final retention payment from the owner.

evidence.quote: All billings for work performed during a calendar month shall be made on Contractor’s standard forms “Progress Payment Request” and “Conditional Waiver and Release Upon Progress Payment”
evidence.rationale: Each monthly billing must be made on a conditional waiver and release form.

evidence.quote: Contractor also reserves the right to require Subcontractor to execute an Unconditional Waiver and Release form as to previously paid progress payments if required by the Contract Documents or the Owner.
evidence.rationale: This is a reserved right, triggered only if the Contract Documents or the Owner require it, rather than an automatic requirement.

evidence.quote: Contractor reserves the right to require mechanics’ lien, stop notice, construction lien, materialman and bond claim releases (including releases from lower tier subcontractors) and payment affidavits in duplicate with each application for progress payments and on final payment.
evidence.rationale: Lower-tier releases may be required at Contractor's election.

evidence.quote: Contractor reserves the right to make payment by joint check or by direct check to Subcontractor’s materialmen or sub-subcontractors
evidence.rationale: Joint check payment is expressly reserved.

evidence.quote: Unless prohibited by Law, Contractor may set-off against the Subcontract Price the amounts owing from Subcontractor to Contractor, whether or not relating to the project.
evidence.rationale: An express setoff right appears in 16(b), along with backcharge rights elsewhere (clean-up, bonds).

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold or, on account of subsequently discovered evidence, may nullify, the whole or part of any payment to protect Contractor from loss on account of (1) defective work not remedied
evidence.rationale: An express withholding right for defective work and claims appears in 6(f).

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise provided in the Contract Documents, payments will be made on account of materials or equipment not incorporated in the Work but delivered and suitably stored at the site
evidence.rationale: On-site stored materials are payable unless the Contract Documents provide otherwise. Off-site storage requires that the Contract Documents allow it and that Contractor approve it in advance, plus title documentation.

anomalies.description: Payment is limited to a special fund consisting of owner payments. The subcontractor effectively bears the risk of owner non-payment, which is pay-if-paid language.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor understands that all payments to Subcontractor will be made only from a special fund and a specific source, namely, from payments made by Owner from time to time to Contractor in respect of work performed by Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Payment is limited to a special fund consisting of owner payments. The subcontractor effectively bears the risk of owner non-payment, which is pay-if-paid language.

anomalies.description: If the owner does not pay (including owner insolvency), the subcontractor's right to payment is conditioned on Contractor first exhausting litigation and appeals to final judgment. This could defer payment indefinitely.

evidence.quote: then Subcontractor’s right to payment shall be conditioned upon the passage of such time as may be reasonable and necessary for Contractor to fully exercise and exhaust to final judgment its legal, extra judicial and appellate rights and remedies
evidence.rationale: If the owner does not pay (including owner insolvency), the subcontractor's right to payment is conditioned on Contractor first exhausting litigation and appeals to final judgment. This could defer payment indefinitely.

anomalies.description: The surety and Contractor may assert non-payment by the owner as a defense to the subcontractor's bond claims.

evidence.quote: the nonoccurrence of any conditions to payments set forth in this Subcontract, including without limitation the failure or delay of payment to Contractor.
evidence.rationale: The surety and Contractor may assert non-payment by the owner as a defense to the subcontractor's bond claims.

anomalies.description: Receipt of releases and affidavits, and Contractor's approval of them, are conditions precedent to any payment.

evidence.quote: Receipt by Contractor of all required releases and affidavits, and approval by Contractor of those documents, are conditions precedent to payment by Contractor to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Receipt of releases and affidavits, and Contractor's approval of them, are conditions precedent to any payment.

anomalies.description: The contract requires Contractor's own standard waiver forms and refuses other forms. It does not reference the California statutory waiver forms (Civil Code 8132-8138).

evidence.quote: No other form of payment request will be accepted.
evidence.rationale: The contract requires Contractor's own standard waiver forms and refuses other forms. It does not reference the California statutory waiver forms (Civil Code 8132-8138).

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on final acceptance by the Architect and Owner and on Contractor's receipt of final retention from the Owner. Release is tied to owner action, not the subcontractor's own completion.

evidence.quote: until after final acceptance of the work by the Architect and Owner and until ten (10) days after Contractor’s receipt of final retention payment from Owner
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on final acceptance by the Architect and Owner and on Contractor's receipt of final retention from the Owner. Release is tied to owner action, not the subcontractor's own completion.

anomalies.description: The setoff right is unusually broad. It extends to retainage and to amounts owed under other contracts, including contracts with subsidiaries or affiliates, whether or not related to the Project.

evidence.quote: offset and apply any amounts due Contractor as a result of such default against any earned but unpaid amounts owing to Subcontractor by Contractor under the Subcontract, including without limitation, any retainage held by Contractor
evidence.rationale: The setoff right is unusually broad. It extends to retainage and to amounts owed under other contracts, including contracts with subsidiaries or affiliates, whether or not related to the Project.

anomalies.description: Amounts withheld after a default, including sums due under other contracts, accrue no interest.

evidence.quote: whether related to the Project or otherwise and during such period such withheld amounts shall not accrue interest
evidence.rationale: Amounts withheld after a default, including sums due under other contracts, accrue no interest.

anomalies.description: Withholding grounds include subjective 'reasonable doubt' triggers and any ground 'otherwise provided' in the Subcontract.

evidence.quote: reasonable doubt that the work under this Agreement can be completed for the balance of the Subcontract Price then unpaid
evidence.rationale: Withholding grounds include subjective 'reasonable doubt' triggers and any ground 'otherwise provided' in the Subcontract.

anomalies.description: Payment for stored materials is conditioned on procedures satisfactory to Contractor, which is a discretionary standard. It can also be overridden by the Contract Documents.

evidence.quote: or such other procedures satisfactory to Contractor to establish Owner’s title to such materials or equipment
evidence.rationale: Payment for stored materials is conditioned on procedures satisfactory to Contractor, which is a discretionary standard. It can also be overridden by the Contract Documents.

anomalies.description: Contractor alone determines the manner of payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor agrees that Contractor shall have the right to determine the manner in which payment shall be made.
evidence.rationale: Contractor alone determines the manner of payment.

anomalies.description: There is no fixed deadline for payment applications. Applications must be early enough not to delay Contractor's own billing to the Owner.

evidence.quote: Payment requests must be delivered to Contractor sufficiently early as to not delay timely submission of Contractor’s progress payment requests to Owner.
evidence.rationale: There is no fixed deadline for payment applications. Applications must be early enough not to delay Contractor's own billing to the Owner.

anomalies.description: Prime Contract Documents are incorporated, and conflicts are resolved by the provision most stringent on the Subcontractor. Payment terms in the Prime Contract (not provided) could alter these rules.

evidence.quote: the provision imposing the most stringent obligation on the part of the Subcontractor will control.
evidence.rationale: Prime Contract Documents are incorporated, and conflicts are resolved by the provision most stringent on the Subcontractor. Payment terms in the Prime Contract (not provided) could alter these rules.
